questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between the Merge transformation and the Merge Join transformation?
options: Merge stacks two same-shaped sorted datasets into one; Merge Join actually joins two sorted datasets column-wise
Merge supports more than two inputs, while Merge Join is limited to exactly two
Merge Join requires unsorted input, while Merge requires sorted input
There is no real difference — they are two names for the same transformation
questions.explain: Merge combines two sorted datasets with matching column shapes into a single dataset (similar to Union All). Merge Join produces wider rows by joining two sorted datasets on key columns using FULL, LEFT, or INNER join logic.

questions.q: When should you use Union All instead of the Merge transformation?
options: When the inputs aren't sorted, the output doesn't need to be sorted, or there are more than two inputs
Only when working with string columns
Only when the two inputs come from the same table
Never — Union All and Merge are always interchangeable
questions.explain: Microsoft's own guidance is to use Union All instead of Merge when inputs are unsorted, the combined output doesn't need sorting, or there are more than two inputs — Merge only ever takes exactly two.

questions.q: Which three join types does the Merge Join transformation support?
options: FULL, LEFT, and INNER
LEFT, RIGHT, and CROSS
INNER, CROSS, and SELF
FULL, RIGHT, and OUTER ANTI
questions.explain: The Merge Join Transformation Editor lets you specify a FULL, LEFT (outer), or INNER join between its two sorted inputs.

questions.q: What requirement do both Merge and Merge Join share for their inputs?
options: Both require sorted data on the merge/join columns
Both require a Cache connection manager
Both require exactly one input and one output
Both require the inputs to come from an OLE DB source specifically
questions.explain: Both transformations require sorted data for their inputs — this is exactly why the Sort transformation (Lesson 24) matters so much before either of these runs.

questions.q: How does Merge Join differ from a Lookup transformation, even though both add columns based on matching keys?
options: Merge Join works directly with two data flow inputs and natively supports outer joins, with no reference dataset or caching modes involved
Merge Join can only perform exact-match joins, while Lookup supports fuzzy matching
Lookup requires sorted inputs, while Merge Join does not
Merge Join is only available in the Azure Data Factory SSIS Integration Runtime
questions.explain: Lookup joins a data flow input against a separate reference dataset with configurable caching. Merge Join instead joins two live data flow inputs directly, and natively supports FULL/LEFT/INNER outer join semantics.
